title: 2016 AMC 12B 18
statement: What is the area of the region enclosed by the graph of the equation \(x^2+y^2=|x|+|y|?\)

solutions.text:
By symmetry, consider the first quadrant, where the equation is \(x^2+y^2=x+y,\) or \(\left(x-\tfrac12\right)^2+\left(y-\tfrac12\right)^2=\tfrac12.\) This is a circle centered at \(\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\) passing through \((1,0)\) and \((0,1);\) since the center is the midpoint of that chord, the enclosed first-quadrant region is the right triangle with legs to \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\) (area \(\tfrac12\)) plus a semicircle of radius \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\) (area \(\dfrac\pi4\)). Multiplying by \(4\) for all quadrants gives \(4\left(\tfrac12+\tfrac\pi4\right)=\pi+2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The graph is symmetric about both axes; in the first quadrant the equation is \(x^2+y^2=x+y\)
Complete the square to \(\left(x-\tfrac12\right)^2+\left(y-\tfrac12\right)^2 =\tfrac12;\) in that quadrant the region is a right triangle plus a semicircle
